Our paper examining how smoking and vaping acutely affect vascular function has been published in the *[Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging](https://doi.org/10.1002/jmri.70403)*.

## Summary

E-cigarettes are often considered a safer alternative to tobacco, but their acute vascular effects are not well understood — particularly when measured across multiple vascular beds simultaneously. In this prospective study, we recruited 41 smokers/vapers and 17 non-smokers/non-vapers and scanned each participant pre- and post-challenge on three separate days, using either tobacco cigarettes (t-cigs), nicotinized e-cigarettes (e-cigs⁺), or non-nicotinized e-cigarettes (e-cigs⁻). Using 3T quantitative MRI (oximetry and blood flow velocimetry), we characterized changes in femoral artery blood flow velocity waveforms at rest and in response to cuff occlusion — providing a more comprehensive picture of acute vascular response than a single physiological endpoint can offer.

## Citation

> Nabbout, M., Hosseini, M., Quach, H., Langham, M. C., Caporale, A. S., Guo, W., et al. (2026). Acute effects of smoking and vaping on markers of vascular function via quantitative MRI. *Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging*. https://doi.org/10.1002/jmri.70403
